about: The words the one said-as reader (src/english/said-as.ts) says a person, an office and a job with, and the telling's clock and budgets (src/english/telling.ts). Words composer, part 1 and 2 (docs/design/words-composer.md, Nov 12). A person is said by role and name the first time a text says them, then by the role, a pronoun or their first name; an office's words come from its record's office kind; a job held outside the town is said the way people say it, never as a title.

eveningFromMinute.checkedAgainst: 5:00 PM, as src/director/data/scene-talk-rules.json timeOfDay.eveningFromMinute: from then a line looking ahead says tomorrow, never tonight.

fullName.checkedAgainst: Owner, Nov 12: no full name twice on one screen ("saying the full name every time").

subject.checkedAgainst: Words skill, Nov 11: a subject's word at most three times in one speech or scene.

they.about: Someone with no he or she on record is said again as they (src/english/said-as.ts wordPersonSlots), never by their role twice in one line (owner, Nov 12: "There needs to be pronouns and titles"). A line's verbs are written for one person, so the word after they ("knows" to "know") and a question's verb before it ("does" to "do") take the plural.

outsideJob.about: A job the residents engine fills in for a commuter, held with the outside market that stands in for work out of town: its title ("Works outside the town") is a placeholder, never said as a job.
outsideJob.title: Works outside the town

federal.about: How talk says the federal government (src/director/conversation.ts pointSubject): by its capital, or plainly in a state that goes by the capital's name (composed-checks.json placeSaidOnlyAs), so "whatever Washington says" never means the state (owner, Nov 12: "Which Washington?").
federal.name: Washington

deciders.about: Who decides a question, by its level, said in talk where a line names who should act (never 'somebody'; lead, Nov 12).

ownPlace.about: Owner via the coordinator, Nov 12: a district's or employer's name is never spoken as the place someone goes. A student says their own school as 'school'; a worker names the employer once in a talk and then says 'work'. By the tie between the person and the organization.

questionAgain.about: Lead, Nov 12 ("say no to raising the debt limit only with spending cuts to match" right after the opener named it in full): once a line has named a question, its act is said again in a short form, by the slot it fills. Lead, Nov 13: while it is the only question on the table, a later mention of its name in the talk is `it`. Words only; the composer reads them.
